key_results: High-energy XCT quantifies progressive transition from metallic-iron shell (1300°C) to iron-slag coexistence/oxide enrichment (1400°C) to melting/dripping (1550°C); moving particle hydrodynamics reproduces pellet-layer densification, narrowing, and collapse using yield-stress formulation; inverse calibration derives temperature-dependent shell-strength law
comments: Integration of 3D tomography with particle simulations bridging static imaging to predictive multiscale furnace models is innovative; scalability to heterogeneous real-burden materials and dynamic gas flow coupling remains to be demonstrated.

model_io.model: Reduced iron ore pellet in cohesive zone
outputs: particle displacement and collapse via moving particle hydrodynamics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Internal transformation of reduced pellets (metallic shell → iron-slag → melt) governs mechanical collapse of packed bed
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: tomographic images reveal progressive structural evolution; particle simulations using DFT-calibrated yield-stress reproduce observed collapse; inverse calibration yields predictive shell-strength model

title: Dual-band single negative metamaterial-based MIMO antenna with enhanced performance
task: Dual-band metamaterial MIMO antenna for wideband circular polarization
key_results: Single-layer metasurface converts narrowband linear to wideband circular polarization; impedance bandwidth 3.11 GHz (4.3–7.41 GHz); axial ratio bandwidth 1.6 GHz; gain 4.8–7.8 dB
comments: Dual-band SNG properties (negative ε in 3–5.9 GHz, negative μ in 5.9–9 GHz) enable antenna miniaturization, but practical multiplexing performance in crowded RF environments needs assessment.

model_io.model: Metasurface-integrated MIMO antenna with grounded dielectric substrate

title: Beamstop-free small-angle X-ray scattering for multiscale structure measurement of high-energy-density plasma
task: Beamstop-free small-angle X-ray scattering for multiscale plasma structure measurement at high-energy density
key_results: Layered metallic filter-based beamstop-free SAXS system achieves wide q-range acquisition including critical small-angle region; resolved microscale and macroscale rarefaction dynamics in submicron columnar plasmas; plasma scale length identified as key parameter governing laser absorption; single-shot multiscale measurement enabled
comments: Innovative hardware approach (filters replacing beamstop) overcomes SAXS measurement gap; application to filamentation and turbulence in stochastic HED plasmas shows promise but requires validation of filter calibration stability under extreme conditions.

model_io.model: High-energy-density plasma from high-intensity laser on silicon rod array

hypotheses.hypothesis: Plasma scale length governs laser absorption efficiency in structured targets
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via beamstop-free SAXS: microscale and macroscale rarefaction dynamics resolved in single shot; initial scale length identified as critical parameter

title: Levitodynamics beyond the ground state of motion
task: Prospects and future directions for optically levitated mechanical systems beyond ground-state cooling
key_results: Perspective on two key research areas: precision sensing and generation of non-classical mechanical states; identifies technological applications and foreseeable challenges
comments: Timely forward-looking review after ground-state cooling milestone; roadmap synthesis useful for community but inherently speculative regarding technological readiness.
